# 0058. Third-party licence notices generated by cargo-about

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2026-10-21
- Deciders: maintainers

## Context
Installers and archives distribute PhotoSquirrel in binary form, so every bundled component's licence notice has to
travel with them. The dependency graph of the two shipped binaries has about 650 crates under some 25 licences,
among them `mozjpeg-sys` (`IJG AND Zlib AND BSD-3-Clause`: the IJG README asks binary distributions to say the
software is "based in part on the work of the Independent JPEG Group", and the libjpeg-turbo BSD and Zlib notices
must be reproduced). A hand-kept notices file would drift from `Cargo.lock` with every dependency update.

## Decision
`cargo xtask package` runs `cargo about generate --format json` (cargo-about 0.9.2, a build tool installed by CI
and the Linux packaging image, not a dependency of any crate) for `photosquirrel` and `photosquirrel-cli` with the
repository's `about.toml`, which lists the accepted licences, the release targets and clarifications for crates
without a licence field. xtask merges the two reports, leaves out PhotoSquirrel's own crates and writes a plain-text
`THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES`: an overview, the IJG acknowledgement, then each distinct licence text with the crates it
covers. Packaging fails if a crate has a licence not in `about.toml`, if the notices lack mozjpeg-sys under any of
IJG, Zlib and BSD-3-Clause, or if a finished package (archive, .deb, AppImage, DMG, NSIS installer) does not contain
the file. The file sits next to the binaries in archives and on Windows, in `/usr/lib/photosquirrel` on Linux and
in `Contents/Resources` in the macOS app bundle.

## Alternatives considered
- **cargo-about's handlebars template output** - needs one invocation per binary and a merge anyway; rendering in
  xtask keeps the format and the checks in one tested place.
- **cargo-deny / cargo-license** - list licences but do not collect the licence texts with copyright lines.
- **A committed notices file checked in CI** - noisy diffs on every lockfile change for no benefit.

## Consequences
- Adding a dependency under a new licence fails packaging until the licence is reviewed and added to `about.toml`.
- `rawler` is LGPL-2.1 and is linked statically. The complete source of PhotoSquirrel is public, so users can
  rebuild against a modified rawler; the notice says so by including the LGPL text.

## Revisit when
cargo-about changes its JSON format, or a dependency requires a NOTICE file beyond its licence text.
